## Cycle Life and Stationary Storage

Sodium-ion batteries are considered a cost-effective candidate for stationary energy storage, though they currently face challenges with inferior cycle life compared to lithium-ion technologies\. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.24683)

Lithium iron phosphate is a specific lithium-ion cathode chemistry often utilized in stationary energy storage systems where operational longevity is prioritized through moderate C-rates and ambient temperature management\. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15440)

No direct head-to-head comparison of cycle life between sodium-ion and lithium iron phosphate under identical stationary grid conditions is established in the provided sources\. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.24683)

## Low-Temperature Performance

Low-temperature operation in lithium-ion systems, including those using lithium iron phosphate, can lead to charge-transfer bottlenecks, lithium plating, and accelerated degradation, significantly reducing service life\. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15440)

The provided material does not contain direct evidence or comparative data regarding the low-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries in stationary grid applications\. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.24683)

## Uncertainty and Further Reading

The retrieved literature cannot establish a quantitative performance ranking between sodium-ion and lithium iron phosphate because the sources focus on distinct development stages and different technical challenges\. [5](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.04963)

Further research into polyanionic cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries is ongoing to address capacity fading and electrolyte instability, which are critical for future stationary storage viability\. [6](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19299)
